title: In silico functional, structural, and pathogenicity assessment of single nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SOX9 gene.
authors: Shadhin, Md Saklain Tanver; Mia, Md Sohel; Das Topu, Tomal Krishno; Tanmoy, Md Shahed Imam; Aktar, Shoab; Sultana, Jannat; Hossen, Faisul; Pranto, Abdur Rahman; Tahsin, Nowmee; Shahir, Nafis Fuad; Talukder, Md Enamul Kabir
one_liner_zh: 该文通过序列与结构计算及MD模拟评估SOX9基因SNP对蛋白结构稳定性的影响，虽涉及TF-DNA结合域突变，但未直接建模TF-DNA互作，方法可迁移至本课题。
abstract: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) play a crucial role in the genetic basis of various human diseases and have the potential to serve as valuable biomarkers for disease prediction and personalized treatment. SNPs alter the genetic sequence that produce muted gene and subsequently mutated gene encode altered amino acid residues that can produce the misfolded protein. The SRY-box transcription factor 9, also known as SOX9, is a key determinant for cell growth and has a significant impact on the development of breast cancer. The molecular mechanisms by which missense SNPs in SOX9 influence the Wnt/beta-catenin signalling pathway and contribute to tumour development in SOX9 members remain poorly understood and require further elucidation. Therefore, various computational methods based on sequence and structure were employed to investigate how mutations affect the SOX9 protein. We identified 5,029 SNPs in the SOX9 gene, of which 1,158 were missense (23.03%), 494 were synonymous (9.82%), and 3,377 were intronic (67.15%). SIFT analysis predicted that nine mutations were deleterious. Seven of these missense SNPs (D85H, F154L, A158T, H165Y, K173E, D441N, and G457D) were found to be damaging, potentially harmful, effective, disease-related, and highly deleterious. A high-risk mutation D85H located within the SOX9 DNA-binding HMG box domain PF00505 suggests a potential role in disease causation. Further, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation revealed variations in RMSD and RMSF values, with higher rGyr and hydrogen bond counts in the mutant protein compared to the wild-type, indicating that the mutation might alter protein structure and stability. Finally, PCA, DCCM, and FEL analyses of SOX9 apo protein and mutated D85H provided detailed insights into primary movements, internal motions, energy landscapes, and structural flexibility. Overall, these findings highlight pathways for further investigation into how missense SNPs in the SOX9 gene modify protein structure and function, potentially aiding in strategies to mitigate the negative consequences of these mutations in humans.
abstract_zh: 单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）在多种人类疾病的遗传基础中扮演着关键角色，并有可能作为疾病预测和个性化治疗的有价值生物标志物。SNPs改变遗传序列，产生沉默基因，随后突变基因编码改变的氨基酸残基，可能导致蛋白质错误折叠。SRY-box转录因子9，也称为SOX9，是细胞生长的关键决定因素，并对乳腺癌的发展具有显著影响。SOX9中错义SNPs影响Wnt/β-catenin信号通路并促进SOX9成员肿瘤发展的分子机制仍知之甚少，需要进一步阐明。因此，采用基于序列和结构的多种计算方法来研究突变如何影响SOX9蛋白。我们在SOX9基因中鉴定出5,029个SNPs，其中1,158个为错义突变（23.03%），494个为同义突变（9.82%），3,377个为内含子突变（67.15%）。SIFT分析预测九个突变具有有害性。其中七个错义SNPs（D85H、F154L、A158T、H165Y、K173E、D441N和G457D）被发现具有破坏性、潜在有害性、有效性、疾病相关性和高度有害性。位于SOX9 DNA结合HMG盒结构域PF00505内的高风险突变D85H提示其在疾病发生中可能发挥作用。此外，分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟显示RMSD和RMSF值存在变异，突变蛋白的rGyr和氢键数量高于野生型，表明突变可能改变蛋白质结构和稳定性。最后，对SOX9 apo蛋白和突变型D85H的PCA、DCCM和FEL分析提供了关于主要运动、内部运动、能量景观和结构灵活性的详细见解。总体而言，这些发现为进一步研究SOX9基因中错义SNPs如何修饰蛋白质结构和功能提供了途径，可能有助于制定策略以减轻这些突变在人类中的负面后果。
